items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1959-12-09
items.q: Clarence Williams' brother played the bass in the band

ctx.x: office. Well yes you told me about that once you had your own band. That's the time Clarence

Williams' brother played the bass in the band and George Lewis. A fella in the name of Buddy Brunson. That man had the funniest lip I ever seen. I don't know what kind of trombone that he had. An E flat tenor trombone or something. A high one, a little one. Yeah. With the valve. With the valve. And he didn't know even how to tune but he could play it. You know what he'd do? He'd sound the air on the violin you know. And he'd finger any one of them valves, and he'd be flat that way he'd blow it up. He'd say, and…
I want to ask a little bit about Vincent again. How did he play? Did he ever take the slide trombone later? Do you remember?

items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1958-06-19, 20
items.q: I got a job for him and Clarence William and Paul... So they all went down and worked at this house together. They had a nice band.

ctx.x: Do you think that Brunk imitated Buddy Petite?

No he didn't imitate, he was a better cornet player in Buddy Petite I think. Brunk was a better cornet player than Buddy Petite. He knew a little something about music you see. Uh huh. And Buddy didn't know nothing about music. That made Brunk the best. Did you ever play in the same band with Bunk any place? Oh yeah I played around there with him on jobs, you know, a little gig job some time. I played with him in Alexandria. And got a job for him, got a job for him and Clarence William and Paul, a fellow with…
The violin? Wasn't he with Handy once too?
